To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the response of conduit arteries to flow is heterogeneous and dependent on the characteristics (duration and magnitude) of the flow stimulus; 2) dilatation in the presence of short periods of flow is nitric oxide– dependent, whereas dilatations during sustained flow stimuli are not; and 3) hypercholesterolaemia selectively impairs the nitric oxide pathway.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the endothelium of human conduit arteries is heterogeneous in its response to blood flow and that this heterogeneity is relevant to endothelial function in hypercholesterolaemia.

endothelium-dependent dilatation of conduit arteries is mediated by a complex interaction between multiple endothelial mediators, and the relative importance of these mediators depends on the characteristics of flow stimulus.

FMD is a complex phenomenon, which is dependent on an integrated response of the endothelial cells to blood flow.

endothelial function is not a single phenomenon.
